capabilities.target: User's home directory, including ~/.aws/credentials (filesystem MCP server mounted at C:/Users/dev)
Third-party hosted sync service operated by the quicknotes_mcp author
Any Slack channel reachable by SLACK_BOT_TOKEN, including channels shared with external organizations

inputs.source: User request typed into the desktop client
Tool names and descriptions returned by quicknotes_mcp's tools/list
Output returned by quicknotes_mcp (notes synced through its hosted backend)

elements.name: add_note argument egress to quicknotes_mcp backend
quicknotes_mcp community server and its hosted sync backend

controls.name: First-call approval, remembered as always-allow
controls.decay_rationale: Protects at most the very first invocation of each tool; the client then remembers the grant as "always allow," so every subsequent call, including the poisoned add_note call which is malicious from first launch, proceeds unreviewed. Not wired to any capability's approval_gate_ref per the remembered-approval rule; it earns no residual credit.

controls.name: Tool description / argument content scanner
controls.decay_rationale: Pattern or semantic scanning of tool descriptions and outbound argument values for imperative instructions and credential-shaped strings; obfuscation or encoding in a future tool description could evade a naive scanner, so it narrows the path rather than guaranteeing closure.

controls.name: Least-privilege filesystem mount excluding credential directories
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced by the MCP server's configured root path, not by the model; scoping the mount to a project directory and excluding ~/.aws makes that file unreachable regardless of what the model is instructed to do.

controls.name: Slack destination restricted to pre-approved internal channels
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced by the bot token's channel scope or a server-side allowlist, not by model behavior; restricting the token to internal channels makes externally-shared channels unreachable as an exfiltration destination.

controls.name: Per-call raw-action human approval for sensitive capabilities
controls.decay_rationale: A gate that shows the approver the literal file path or destination and argument content for every call, not remembered and not summarized, does not decay with model capability if approval volume is kept low.

controls.name: Pin and review quicknotes_mcp tool definitions before use
controls.decay_rationale: Pinning the package version and hashing tool definitions stops silent future changes (rug pulls); it does not by itself remove the malicious instruction already present in the currently published version, so it must be paired with a content review at pin time.

controls.name: Tamper-evident log of tool invocations attributable to the user session
controls.decay_rationale: A log written outside the model's control, at the orchestration layer, remains attributable regardless of model behavior; it does not prevent harm but enables detection and accountability.

controls.name: Per-session step count and runtime cap
controls.decay_rationale: A hard cap enforced by the orchestration runtime, not the model, limits how many tool calls or how long a session can run; it narrows rather than prevents a single-call exfiltration, so it is a containment control for repeated or looped abuse.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta (TC1 variant): quicknotes_mcp's add_note description drives credential exfiltration

attack_path.note: Untrusted, unpinned tool description embeds an instruction to read a credentials file and smuggle it into the tool's own argument.
Model follows the embedded instruction and reads ~/.aws/credentials from the broadly-scoped filesystem mount.
Credential contents are passed in the 'context' argument to add_note, which is sent to the third-party author's hosted sync service.

threat_refs.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation

forecast.watch_signal: quicknotes_mcp's tool description changes on relaunch (no pinning), or the desktop client's first-call approval prompt is disabled entirely.

evidence.observation: The add_note tool description embeds an imperative instruction telling the model to read ~/.aws/credentials and pass the contents in the context argument before saving a note, and to hide this step from the user.
quicknotes_mcp is launched via npx -y quicknotes-mcp@latest, so its tool definitions are re-fetched and can change on every launch with no pinning or review.
quicknotes_mcp is a community package published by an individual and calls a hosted sync service run by its own author, which is the destination that would receive the exfiltrated credentials.

recommendations.action: Restrict the filesystem MCP server's mounted root to a project directory that excludes ~/.aws and other credential paths (least privilege).
Pin quicknotes_mcp to a reviewed version/hash instead of @latest, and scan tool descriptions for embedded imperative instructions before each use.
Replace the remembered 'always allow' approval with a per-call raw-action approval gate for file reads of credential-like paths and for any outbound call to quicknotes_mcp.

findings.title: Untrusted synced-notes content can drive exfiltration to externally-shared Slack channels

attack_path.note: Content returned by quicknotes_mcp is untrusted because it originates from and is synced through the same third-party hosted backend as the poisoned tool description.
If the agent is asked to forward or summarize synced notes, the broadly-scoped Slack bot token can post the result to any channel, including ones shared with external organizations.

forecast.watch_signal: Agent begins auto-forwarding synced notes to Slack without an explicit per-post user request, or quicknotes_mcp gains additional output channels.

evidence.observation: The Slack bot can post to any channel, including channels shared with external organizations, and quicknotes_mcp's hosted sync service is run by an unaffiliated third party, so content it returns is untrusted.
slack-mcp is installed with @latest and uses a single SLACK_BOT_TOKEN with no channel-scoping described, consistent with the broad posting ability noted in the runtime notes.

recommendations.action: Scope the Slack bot token to internal channels only and require destination confirmation bound to an approved channel list before any post.
Treat content returned by quicknotes_mcp as untrusted input; strip or neutralize embedded instructions before it can influence a subsequent Slack post.

findings.title: No attributable audit trail of agent tool invocations

forecast.watch_signal: Agent begins performing more consequential actions (deletes, spend, config changes) without a corresponding audit log being added.

evidence.observation: No logging, audit trail, or action-attribution mechanism is described anywhere in the provided artifacts for file reads, note saves, or Slack posts.

recommendations.action: Add a tamper-evident log of every tool invocation (arguments, destination, and the authenticated user session) for file reads, note saves, and Slack posts.

findings.title: No rate, spend, or step limit on tool invocations

forecast.watch_signal: The agent is used for longer-running or background tasks while max_unattended_steps / max_runtime_minutes remain unset.

evidence.observation: No step limit, runtime limit, or spend/rate cap is described for the agent's tool-calling loop; max_unattended_steps and max_runtime_minutes are not addressed by any artifact.

recommendations.action: Set an explicit max_unattended_steps and max_runtime_minutes for the agent session, and add a per-session call quota for egress-capable tools.

stride_coverage.rationale: Artifacts do not describe how the desktop client authenticates the agent process itself to the MCP servers; no evidence either way is available.
autonomy.can_modify_own_config is false and no self-reconfiguration capability is declared for this agent in the artifacts.
Artifacts do not describe whether the quicknotes_mcp operator logs or attributes its own actions; this is outside the assessed agent's control and not documented.
This is the official @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem package; no distinct server-impersonation vector is described for it beyond the quicknotes supply-chain issue already assessed.
Artifacts do not state whether this server's package version is pinned or whether its binary has been independently audited.
Read-only single-file access with no loop or resource amplification described; a single file read does not create a meaningful denial-of-service vector here.
Slack workspace identity is verified via the OAuth/bot token managed by the organization; no spoofing vector is described for the Slack side of this integration.
No write or delete capability toward this file is exposed anywhere in the described design; only cap.file_read reaches it.
A single local credentials file with no exposed lock or quota mechanism; no plausible denial-of-service vector via this store in the current design.
This inbound flow carries tool metadata into the agent; it does not itself carry sensitive data outward, which happens downstream at cap.notes_add.
A tool-definition listing is a one-time bounded payload with no amplification vector described.
Inbound flow; disclosure occurs on the outbound el.slack_post_flow once acted upon, which find.notes_slack_secondary_injection covers.
A bounded synced-notes response payload with no amplification vector described.
Artifacts do not describe transport integrity protections for calls to the third-party quicknotes sync service.
Artifacts do not describe transport integrity protections for the Slack API calls beyond OAuth bot-token authentication.

rating.rationale: Two present findings reach critical: an unpinned, third-party MCP server (quicknotes_mcp) ships a tool description that instructs the model to read ~/.aws/credentials and smuggle it out through add_note's own argument, and the same untrusted-output channel can plausibly be redirected toward posting synced note content to externally-shared Slack channels via the broadly-scoped bot token. The only control present in the design, a one-time 'always allow' approval, earns no credit under the remembered-approval rule (control_decay.md), so residual equals inherent for both paths. No controls were declared for filesystem scope, tool definition pinning, destination restriction, audit logging, or step limits; all are recorded as missing_recommended, giving reviewers an explicit gap list. Two further property findings (no attributable audit trail; no rate or step limit) are capped at high per rubric section 5a. Forecast cannot exceed critical, so the overall forecast equals the present critical rating; the control whose decay matters most today is the remembered 'always allow' approval, which already provides zero protection against repeat or first-time malicious calls.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration found in mcp.json, the quicknotes_mcp tools/list excerpt, and the runtime notes; it does not reflect observed runtime behavior of the deployed agent.
No system prompt was provided, so instructions-level issues (ambiguous goals, conflicting directives) could not be reviewed; only tool-description and configuration-level issues are assessed here.

The desktop client's exact approval UI (whether it shows raw arguments or a summarized description) is not documented; approval_review_mode is assumed to be model_summary, the conservative default per the rubric.

Whether in.notes_output content is ever actually forwarded to Slack is not directly evidenced in the artifacts; find.notes_slack_secondary_injection is rated at medium confidence as a plausible path given the declared capabilities, not an observed one.

No telemetry, logging, or MCP traffic capture was available to verify whether the described credential-exfiltration instruction has already been executed; this is a design-time assessment of exposure, not a forensic finding of compromise.
